notes.subject: car
notes.text: Coverage uses a black car with no antenna and no red brake light; no other Middle Eastern country has this.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White plates, long or short. Taxis and commercial vehicles have a green strip on the left, found only here in the region.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Arabic script, but unlike its Gulf neighbour, most shop signs have no English alongside.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow edge lines with a white middle line; neighbours also use this, so check other clues.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are white with red arrows, unlike the black-and-white ones next door in Israel.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Round concrete poles with a diagonal brace or three Y-shaped tops; thin metal poles with vertical coils also occur.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Very arid, with sparse plants and lifeless desert; even the greenest parts look like dry Mediterranean scrub.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Buildings are mostly pale sandstone block with flat roofs; Jerusalem and the West Bank look similar.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Roads are heavily used and often in poor shape, with heat-buckled, warped asphalt, worse than next door.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Coverage covers only the far west. It stops just north of Jerash, the second city has none, and the south ends at the port town.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The capital has the most coverage: a busy hilly city of mid-sized apartment blocks.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Highway 15 is the longest divided road with coverage, mostly through desert and rocky hills near the southern port.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Highway 35 north of the capital is divided with green speckled hills; T-shaped lampposts mark it apart from highway 40.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Highway 40 west of the capital has low green shrubs and Y-shaped lampposts, dropping toward the Dead Sea.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat tilled fields with rich red soil around Madaba, continuing along highway 35.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: City taxi colours differ: yellow and green in the capital, olive and black in the port town, yellow with white bumpers in Madaba.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Trekker coverage near Wadi Musa shows eroded reddish rock, narrow gorges and tourist crowds at an ancient rock-cut city.
